PETRA ZLATARIĆ-NOVOSEL
[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN] | [LOCATION]

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Machine Learning Engineer with experience developing and operating NLP and document AI systems for Croatian-language public administration documents. Delivered document classification serving approximately 15,000 documents per day, built a Croatian named entity recognition model, and implemented model drift monitoring that helped identify and resolve an OCR-related accuracy drop. Hands-on experience with Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, FastAPI, Docker, Azure and MLflow. Also built a personal, non-production retrieval-augmented question-answering demo over Croatian laws.

TECHNICAL SKILLS
Programming and data: Python, pandas, Oracle SQL, PostgreSQL
Machine learning and NLP: PyTorch, scikit-learn, Hugging Face Transformers, spaCy, fastText, sentence-transformers, text classification, named entity recognition, TF-IDF, retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)
Deployment and MLOps: FastAPI, Docker, Azure App Service, Azure ML, Azure Functions, MLflow, Evidently, model serving, model drift monitoring
Data annotation: Label Studio, annotation guidelines, inter-annotator agreement

PROFESSIONAL EXPERIENCE
ML Engineer | Slavonica Document AI | 2023–Present
- Develop document classification and named entity recognition solutions for Croatian public administration documents.
- Built and deployed a scanned-document classifier for 23 classes, achieving 94% accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.91.
- Fine-tuned XLM-R base and served the classifier as a FastAPI service in Docker on Azure App Service, processing approximately 15,000 documents per day.
- Developed a Croatian NER model to identify persons, organisations, OIB numbers, addresses and legal references in administrative text.
- Created an annotated dataset of 4,000 documents, including an annotation guideline; coordination across two annotators achieved an inter-annotator kappa of 0.87.
- Implemented weekly drift reporting for text length, vocabulary and predicted-class distribution, with alerts when PSI exceeded 0.2. Identified a silent client OCR change associated with a 9-point accuracy drop; the issue was fixed within a week.

Data Scientist | Baranjska kreditna banka | 2021–2023
- Developed churn prediction models and complaint classification solutions.
- Built a customer complaint topic classifier, progressing from a TF-IDF and logistic regression baseline to fastText across 11 topics.
- Delivered weekly topic reporting for customer service management.

SELECTED PROJECT
Retrieval-Augmented Question-Answering Demo | Personal project | 2025
- Built a weekend prototype for question answering over Croatian laws using a sentence embedding model and an open-weight LLM accessed through an API.
- Implemented retrieval with FAISS; the prototype was not used in production and was checked manually without formal evaluation.

EDUCATION
Doctoral studies, named entity recognition in Croatian legal texts | University of Drava | Expected 2027

TEACHING AND PUBLICATION
Guest lecturer, NLP Summer School | 2025 | 90-minute lecture
Croatian Named Entity Recognition research published at a regional workshop | 2024

LANGUAGES
English: Used daily in meetings with a client in Slovenia

critique.content_quality_feedback: The CV is clear, well structured, concise, and professionally written. It presents strong evidence of production NLP/document AI work, including measurable results, deployment scale, model quality, annotation quality, and a concrete monitoring incident. The project descriptions are credible and appropriately transparent about the personal RAG demo being non-production. The strongest content is the 15,000-documents-per-day deployment, 94% accuracy, macro F1 of 0.91, kappa of 0.87, and the nine-point accuracy-drop investigation. The main content weaknesses are that the supplied Azure certification is omitted, contact fields remain placeholders, and some job-relevant experience—particularly data versioning, feature engineering, and ingestion pipelines—is not evidenced. These latter points are candidate-profile gaps or unsupported requirements rather than defects that can be solved through wording.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses standard section headings, reverse-chronological experience, readable bullets, and ATS-friendly plain text formatting. Relevant keywords are present, including Python, PyTorch, Hugging Face Transformers, FastAPI, Docker, Azure App Service, Azure ML, MLflow, model serving, model drift monitoring, NLP, NER, text classification, and RAG. The likely ATS screening probability is good to high for NLP/document AI and Azure-focused searches, approximately 80–88%, but lower for this specific role because the CV does not include the exact concepts 'data versioning,' 'feature engineering,' 'data ingestion pipelines,' CI/CD, or automated tests—and the candidate material does not support most of these terms. The certification omission also reduces keyword coverage. Replace the contact placeholders before submission; placeholders may parse as incomplete or unprofessional contact information.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document aligns strongly with the role's core ML engineering, NLP, model serving, monitoring, Python, Azure, and MLflow requirements. The production document-classification service and drift-monitoring work are particularly relevant to building, deploying, and operating AI systems. The RAG requirement is shown, but only through a personal, non-production prototype, so it is a weaker match than production AI-assistant experience. The CV does not establish a completed degree in machine learning, computer science, or a related engineering field; the listed doctoral studies are ongoing and expected in 2027. It also does not establish four years as an ML Engineer shipping production systems: the ML Engineer role is dated 2023–Present, while the earlier Data Scientist role does not explicitly establish production ML deployment. Data versioning, feature engineering, and data-ingestion pipelines are not evidenced in the candidate material. Team collaboration is supported by coordination with two annotators and client-facing work, but the CV provides limited direct evidence for the company's broader culture signals such as service ownership, candid feedback, or cross-functional product collaboration.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL — In the contact header, replace '[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN] | [LOCATION]' with the candidate's actual professional contact details before submitting the CV. Do not leave placeholders in the final document.

CRITICAL — Add a CERTIFICATIONS section, preferably after EDUCATION, with: 'Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate | 2024'. This is supported by the candidate's notes and strengthens the Azure AI/MLOps alignment.

MINOR — In the Professional Summary, retain the accurate qualification of the RAG work but make its relevance easier for ATS and recruiters to identify by changing the final sentence to: 'Built a personal, non-production retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) question-answering prototype over Croatian laws using sentence-transformers, FAISS, and an open-weight LLM API.'

MINOR — In the Selected Project section for the RAG demo, change 'Implemented retrieval with FAISS' to 'Implemented retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with sentence-transformers and FAISS, using an open-weight LLM through an API.' This makes the implementation and the job-ad terminology explicit without implying production experience.

MINOR — In the ML Engineer experience section, make the production engineering keywords more prominent by changing the first two bullets to: '- Develop and operate production document-classification and named entity recognition services for Croatian public administration documents.' and '- Built and deployed a 23-class scanned-document classifier, achieving 94% accuracy and a macro F1 score of 0.91.' This preserves the existing facts while directly reflecting the ad's 'build, deploy and operate' language.
critique.critical_issues:
1. The final CV contains unresolved contact placeholders: '[EMAIL] | [PHONE] | [LINKEDIN] | [LOCATION]'. These must be replaced before submission.
2. The candidate's Azure certification, 'Microsoft Certified: Azure AI Engineer Associate (2024),' is supported by the original candidate information but omitted from the CV, reducing completeness and ATS alignment.
3. No unsupported skills, tools, certifications, or experiences were detected in the current CV. The RAG experience is appropriately described as a personal, non-production prototype.

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a strong, well-structured CV with clear specialization in NLP, document AI and production machine learning. The CV is appropriately transparent about the personal RAG prototype being non-production and manually checked. The main content weakness is that it does not explicitly distinguish the candidate's total ML/AI production experience from the four-year requirement, and it does not provide a completed degree. It also gives limited evidence of broader software engineering practices such as data versioning, automated testing, CI/CD, feature engineering and ingestion pipelines.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses conventional section headings, simple text formatting, strong job-relevant keywords and easily parseable bullet points. Estimated AI/ATS screening probability is moderate to high for the technical keywords, approximately 75–85%, but lower for this specific vacancy because the document does not show a degree, four years as an ML Engineer, data versioning, feature engineering or data ingestion pipelines. Do not add unsupported tools such as AWS, Kubernetes, Airflow or CI/CD.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: Alignment is strong for the role's NLP and production AI focus. The customer complaint classification background is also relevant to customer-support AI, although the CV could make that connection more visible. The candidate's material does not establish a completed degree, four years specifically as a Machine Learning Engineer, data versioning, feature engineering or data-ingestion pipeline experience. These are genuine requirement gaps or unverified requirements, not defects that can be solved by rewriting. The RAG experience is shown but is only a personal, non-production prototype, so it is weaker than the job's preferred experience with deployed AI assistants. No unsupported claim about customer-support assistants, LLM fine-tuning, AWS/GCP or orchestration should be introduced.

The CV should not imply these capabilities. Overall, this is a strong adjacent match with meaningful experience gaps against several stated must-haves.

The complaint-classification background also provides a relevant connection to customer-support AI, although the CV does not claim an unsupported production chat assistant. The candidate's material does not establish a completed degree in machine learning, computer science, or a related engineering field; it lists doctoral studies expected in 2027. It also does not establish four years specifically as a machine learning engineer shipping systems to production: the ML Engineer role begins in 2023, while the earlier Data Scientist role is not documented as production ML engineering. Data versioning, feature engineering, and data ingestion pipelines are not evidenced in the candidate material. These are substantive qualification gaps rather than CV-writing defects and should not be presented as accomplishments. The CV aligns well with the company's ownership, pragmatism, learning, and candid problem-solving signals through its operational monitoring example, quantified incident resolution, teaching, publication, and annotation work.
